content:
Hark! Pray what season dost thou intend to traverse the fair lands of Nippon?

If ‘tis spring when cherry blossoms dance upon the breeze then mark these days with care:

Day the First:
Upon the morrow at break of dawn take swift passage to Tokyo’s golden gates.
First to the Imperial Palace where ancient stones do whisper tales of emperors old.
Then to Ueno’s gardens fair where petals blush in softest hue.
As night doth fall take rest at an inn by Asakusa’s river fair.

Day the Second:
To Shibuya’s crossroads bold where throngs do surge like waves upon the sea.
Then to Harajuku’s lanes where youth in colors strange do walk.
Pay homage to Meiji’s shrine where cedars stand in silent prayer.
At eve sup upon sushi fresh by Tsukiji’s auction hall.

Day the Third:
Board the swift Shinkansen to Kyoto’s hallowed ground.
First to Kinkaku-ji where golden pavilion gleams in sun’s embrace.
Then to Arashiyama’s groves where bamboo towers ‘gainst heaven’s face.
Dine upon kaiseki rich as night itself draws nigh.

Day the Fourth:
To Fushimi’s sake shrines where barrels rest in cool dark cellars deep.
Then to Gion’s streets where geisha glide like ghosts in twilight’s keep.
At last to Kiyomizu’s heights where city lights do twinkle bright.
Return to Kyoto’s hearth for rest once more.

Day the Fifth:
Take train to Nara’s ancient ways where deer do bow and temples rise.
First to Todai-ji where Buddha grand doth sit in lotus wise.
Then to Kasuga’s lantern path where stone and light do weave their dance.
As dusk doth fall retire to an inn by Nara’s stream.

If summer’s heat dost call thee then mark these days with care:

Day the First:
To Tokyo return and thither stay.
First to Akihabara’s halls where gadgets gleam and otaku play.
Then to Odaiba’s shores where man-made isles do stretch into the bay.
As stars awake sup upon yakitori’s flame.

Day the Second:
To Nikko’s heights where waterfalls do roar and cedars stand in might.
Then to Toshogu’s shrine where gold and craft do gleam in morning light.
At eve return to Tokyo’s embrace for rest and dream.

Day the Third:
Board the swift Shinkansen to Hiroshima’s shores.
First to Peace Memorial where shadows of war do haunt the air.
Then to Miyajima’s torii where tide doth kiss the sacred gate.
Sup upon okonomiyaki rich and sweet.

Day the Fourth:
To Osaka take swift train and thither feast.
First to Dotonbori’s lights where neon signs do blaze bright.
Then to Osaka Castle where daimyo once did hold their might.
As night doth fall take rest by Namba’s bustling square.

If autumn’s crisp air dost call thee then mark these days with care:

Day the First:
To Kyoto return and thither stay.
First to Ginkaku-ji where silver pavilion gleams in sun’s last rays.
Then to Philosopher’s Path where maples blush in red and gold.
At eve sup upon tofu’s art in Nanzen-ji’s halls.

Day the Second:
To Kurama’s heights where forests whisper secrets old.
Then to Kibune’s shrine where lanterns line the path to heaven’s gate.
Return to Kyoto’s hearth for rest and dream.

Day the Third:
Take train to Kanazawa’s fair where samurai once walked in pride.
First to Kenrokuen’s gardens where autumn paints in hues untold.
Then to Omicho Market where sea’s bounty doth unfold.
As night doth fall retire to an inn by Kanazawa’s keep.

Day the Fourth:
To Takayama take swift train and thither go.
First to Old Town’s lanes where wooden houses stand in time’s embrace.
Then to Hida Folk Village where thatch’d roofs do shelter old Japan.
Sup upon Hida beef rich and tender as the day doth wane.

If winter’s chill doth call thee then mark these days with care:

Day the First:
To Tokyo return and thither stay.
First to teamLab Planets where art doth flow in digital streams.
Then to Roppongi’s halls where night doth sparkle bright.
Sup upon sukiyaki warm and rich by Ginza’s lights.

Day the Second:
To Hakone take swift train and thither go.
First to Owakudani’s vents where sulfurous mists do rise.
Then to Lake Ashi where Mt. Fuji stands in snow-clad guise.
At eve soak in hot springs’ embrace at Gora’s ryokan fair.

Day the Third:
To Nagano take swift train and thither go.
First to Jigokudani’s monkeys where snow doth blanket earth.
Watch as they bathe in waters warm beneath the winter’s breath.
Then to Zenko-ji where lanterns guide the soul to peace profound.

Day the Fourth:
Return to Tokyo’s embrace for rest and dream ere thou dost depart once more.

Thus endeth mine humble counsel for thy journey’s way.
May fortune smile upon thy path and guide thee safe through Nippon’s fair domain.
